what_its_for: Pitolisant is used to treat excessive daytime sleepiness (feeling very sleepy during the day) or cataplexy (sudden muscle weakness or loss of muscle control) in adults who have narcolepsy. Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder that makes it hard to stay awake during the day. Pitolisant works in your brain to help you stay more awake and alert.
how_to_take: Take pitolisant by mouth once every morning when you wake up. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Taking it in the morning helps prevent it from keeping you awake at night. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the dose that works best for you. The usual starting dose is 8.9 mg once daily in the morning. Your doctor may increase your dose to 17.8 mg or up to a maximum of 35.6 mg once daily depending on how you respond and how well you tolerate the medicine. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss your morning dose and you remember it the same morning, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is already afternoon or evening, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose the following morning as usual. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose, as this could cause unwanted side effects.
storage: Store pitolisant at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in your bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you no longer need this medicine or it has expired, ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking pitolisant, as it may increase drowsiness and other side effects. Avoid taking pitolisant together with other medicines that cause QT prolongation (a heart rhythm problem) without talking to your doctor first. Do not start or stop any other medicines, vitamins, or supplements without telling your doctor or pharmacist, as many medicines can interact with pitolisant. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should know that pitolisant can make certain hormonal birth control methods (such as pills, patches, rings, or implants) less effective — use a backup non-hormonal birth control method (like condoms) during treatment and for at least 21 days after stopping pitolisant.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: a fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat or chest pain (these could be signs of a serious heart rhythm problem); signs of a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; mood changes, depression, or thoughts of harming yourself; a positive pregnancy test (pitolisant may harm an unborn baby). Also contact your doctor if you notice nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache, trouble sleeping, or anxiety that bothers you or does not go away.
when_it_works: Pitolisant may start to reduce daytime sleepiness within the first week or two, but it may take several weeks of dose adjustments to get the full benefit. Your doctor will gradually increase your dose over about 7 to 14 weeks to find the right amount for you. Be patient and keep taking the medicine as directed even if you do not notice immediate improvement. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Pitolisant may harm an unborn baby. It is not known if it passes into breast milk, so discuss the risks with your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or monitor you more closely, as your body may process this medicine differently. Older adults: Use pitolisant with caution if you are elderly, as you may be more sensitive to its effects. Children: Pitolisant is not currently approved for use in patients under 18 years of age.
